new_statements.rule_in_words: For all Aru data in Nivens's Proto-Aru database (Ujir included), stress is by default on the penultimate syllable, or on the final syllable when that syllable contains a mid vowel; words deviating from this default are written with an acute accent. In the Ujir forms printed by Grimes & Edwards only three carry the acute (-dʒáŋ, rián, maníʔ, all final stress on a non-mid vowel); the rest are unmarked, i.e. treated as regular penultimate.
new_statements.exceptions: Final stress when the final syllable has a mid vowel (part of the stated default); lexically 'unexpected' stresses marked ad hoc with an acute -- for Ujir: -dʒáŋ 'bite', rián 'ladder', maníʔ 'thin'.
new_statements.domain_note: A transcription convention for citation forms in a comparative wordlist database covering all 14 Aru languages; SECOND-HAND (Grimes & Edwards restating Nivens 2017), not a phonological analysis of Ujir. No first-hand Ujir phonology exists in print as far as could be determined.
new_statements.identity_note: Same variety: the Ujir forms in Grimes & Edwards 2026 come from Antoinette Schapper's fieldwork in Ujir village (ujir1237, ISO udj) as compiled in Nivens's 2017 Proto-Aru database. The stress statement, however, is a database-wide default declared for all 14 Aru languages, not a claim made specifically about Ujir; only three printed Ujir forms are flagged as deviating (final stress: -dʒáŋ, rián, maníʔ).
